rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig`. I read the default-setting text in the authoring and agent-harness chapters (via ripgrep) to see what "omitted settings use defaults" means.

**Builders and fields.** `agent/config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` checks these points:
- `OpenAiConfig::new()` serializes to `{}`, so no field is set by default.
- Chaining `model`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key` and `option` produces exactly the expected serialized fields: `model`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key` and `options`.
- Together these cover the five fields and all six builder methods.

**Trait implementations.**
- `fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` deserializes an OpenAI JSON value, re-serializes it, and requires the same value back. It also round-trips through a string and compares the configs with `assert_eq!`. That covers `Serialize`, `Deserialize` and `PartialEq`.
- `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` compares a deserialized `{"backend":"openai"}` config with `AgentConfig::OpenAi(OpenAiConfig::new())`. `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` calls `OpenAiConfig::default()` and checks its resolved defaults. `assert_eq!` also relies on `Debug`.
- `Clone` and `Debug` are not asserted directly, but neither has behavior of its own that the requirement describes.

**Defaults when settings are omitted.**
- **Model and endpoint:** `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` asserts the resolved model `gpt-6.1-sol` and the resolved endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
- **Inference options:** the same test asserts `max_output_tokens` of 16384 and `reasoning.effort` of `low`.
- **Partial overrides:** `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` covers a user-supplied `max_output_tokens`. It also covers `reasoning` with only `summary`, which gains the default `effort`, and `reasoning` with an explicit `effort`, which is kept.
- **Defaults with a model override:** `configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport]` overrides the model and endpoint. It checks the request body for the overridden model and the default `max_output_tokens` of 16384.
- **Overrides in use:** the same local-transport test sends requests to the configured endpoint with the configured `api_key`.

**Credentials.**
- `fn[openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable]` runs a child test process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. It asserts that `OpenAiConfig::new().resolved_api_key()` returns the value from that variable.
- `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` covers three credential cases. A missing `api_key_env` variable gives an error naming that variable. An explicit `api_key` is returned. Missing or empty environment values are rejected through the `credential` helper.

**Not required here.** The requirement does not say what happens when `option` is called twice with the same key. The overwrite case is tested only for Bedrock, so I did not treat it as a gap. `#[non_exhaustive]` and the public export are checked by `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`, which is marked as a test of `requirements.sdk.public_api`.

I found no plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept.

pub fn api_key_env(self, api_key_env: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key(self, api_key: SecretString) -> Self;

`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.
